title: Release Trellis: Staffing Rotations and Regional Fallback Checkpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist and week-of rollout calendar for the Release Trellis experiment. Focus: compact staffing rotations across UTC regions and an explicit, minimal regional fallback ladder for degraded zones. This doc is intentionally terse — it's a pocket checkpad for on-call/reserve engineers and release coordinators.

Context / TL;DR:
- We want repeatable, low-friction rollouts for small feature batches (<= 5% traffic) across three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-sg).
- Two-tier staffing: primary crew (ops + release lead) and float/reserve (fast escalation for fallbacks).
- Fallback ladder prioritizes routing degrade -> model-variant fallback -> cross-region reroute.

Week-at-a-glance (sprintlet) — April rollout window (example):
- Monday: preflight smoke + dry-run (local canary) 09:00–11:00 PT — preflight owner: Aisha
- Tuesday: regional lab warmup (low-traffic synthetic test) 10:00–12:00 PT — owner: Jordan
- Wednesday: small-batch softlaunch eu-west 08:00–13:00 UTC — primary crew (Marco + Priya + oncall)
- Thursday: us-west progressive ramp 10:00–16:00 PT 
- Friday: ap-sg miniwave 00:00–06:00 SGT (quiet window) 
Notes: shift swaps allowed but must have explicit handoff in #release-ops and update the roll-call doc.

Pre-deploy checklist (must be green before any traffic shift):
- Telemetry smoke: latency P50/P95 dashboards loaded and baseline snapshots captured (link above).
- Canary artifacts: image tagged, hashes verified, canary config pushed to canary namespace.
- Observability hooks: tracing sampling enabled for rollout traces; error budgets flagged to critical thresholds.
- Rollout policy: percent-step plan created (0.5% -> 1% -> 2% -> 5%) and abort thresholds set (error increase > 30% or latency P95 increase > 50ms).
- Oncall: primary + reserve identified, oncall escalation phone numbers in the runbook.
- Communication: Slack #release-ops pinned message prepped; stakeholder email prepared for >10% ramps.

Regional fallback ladder (compact):
1) Local soothe (within-region): reduce route weight to 0.5x for the variant or set circuit-breaker for variant instances.
   - Command notes: terraform apply -target=module.routing.aws_lb_target_group.weight=0.5 (ops helper).
2) Model variant fallback: switch to smaller model-variant with known compatibility (eg rwd-model-v2-small) in the same region.
   - Steps: update variant map in config-store, flush KV-caches that are variant-specific.
   - Quick verify: run /health-check/variant endpoint for top 10 domains.
3) Partial cross-region reroute: shift 10–25% traffic to healthy region (config-driven).
   - Use rollout service: curl -X POST $ROUTE_API/shift -d '{"from":"eu-west","to":"us-west","pct":15}' (wrap in team task).
4) Full region quarantine: if region-level control plane degraded, flip to global fallback (turn off region, route to global steady state).

Escalation & communication matrix:
- t+0 (detection): primary oncall applies Local soothe and posts to #release-ops with incident header.
- t+5 (no improvement): release lead (Marco) invoked; notify product PM + SRE lead; open temporary incident channel.
- t+15: if rollback required, perform variant rollback and start postmortem thread; capture all request traces for the 15 minute window.

Rollout day runbook (hour-by-hour compact for a single region softlaunch):
- H-60: confirm all preflight checks green, post preflight summary to #release-ops.
- H-30: create canary tag and apply ingress rule.
- H-10: start 0.5% traffic shift; monitor.
- H+10: if metrics stable, step to 1%; if not stable, execute local soothe.
- H+30: 2% step. H+60: 5% step if all gates pass.
- Abort pattern: any gate fails -> immediate step down to previous stable step then local soothe; if instability persists, rollback to previous release.

Release notes draft (template + live stub — fill per-release):
- Release title: [short] eg "trellis: compact routing + canary policy tweaks"
- Release date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owner: Marco Chen
- Summary: 1–2 sentences describing user-visible surface (or internal infra changes).
- Changes: bullet list (each item: one-sentence + impact + migration steps if any)
   - e.g. routing: add variant weight decay to minimize cold-start spikes (impact: reduces token latency for new sessions; rollout notes: enabled behind flag).
- Rollout plan: step percentages and regional order.
- Known issues / gotchas: short items and mitigation steps.
- Post-release verification: specific queries / dashboards (include saved query ids).

Post-release verification checklist (first 6 hours):
- Confirm P50/P95 within expected envelope vs baseline (auto snapshot: compare window H+0..H+60).
- Cross-region traffic sanity: no >10% unintended drift.
- Functionality smoke: run 3 scenario prompts across model endpoints.
- Errors: no new 5xx alert clusters.

Retro prompts (to capture immediately after stabilization):
- What went well / what surprised us?
- Which fallbacks were exercised? Why?
- Time-to-decision for critical rollback: how fast did we act?
- Documentation gaps discovered?
- Action items and owners (quick list).

Open questions / TODOs (parking lot):
- Can we automate the first-step local soothe as a safety net (scripted in rollout agent)? (OWNER: Jordan)
- Add a lightweight pager path for product PMs during softlaunch windows (OWNER: Aisha)
- Validate cross-region DNS TTL impacts for ap-sg (OWNER: Priya)

Appendix — quick commands & shortcuts (handy snippets):
- Health probe for variant: curl -s $CONTROL_PLANE/variant/health | jq '.status'
- Shift route (example): curl -X POST $ROUTE_API/shift -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"from":"ap-sg","to":"eu-west","pct":20}'
- Canonical rollback: ops-tool rollback --release trellis-2025-04-08 --confirm

Notes to self / freeform: 
- Keep this doc intentionally compact — for long narratives use the Confluence page linked above.
- We should try a micro-sim next week that exercises fallback ladder in synthetic mode without user traffic.

References / links (quick):
- Confluence: Release Trellis Overview (above)
- Jira: RINF-3421 (progressive rollout engine), RINF-3490 (routing heatmap work)
- GitHub: PR 1983 (canary controller changes)

End of draft.

Quick change log for this doc:

- 2025-04-09: added regional ladder and hour-by-hour runbook (Jordan)
- 2025-04-10: added escalation matrix + open questions (Aisha)
